# When the Gazebo Fortress skid-steer example primarily moves straight and occasionally turns 90° on Ubuntu Focal, what should be verified first?

> **Current answer:** The thread first verifies `libdart` in the original environment, which was 6.9.2-2build4. The maintainer believes that the friction support in the Focal system DART is different from the Gazebo DART fork used in Bionic, and suggests using Bionic, building the fork from source with Ignition, or using the dartsim PPA for version A/B. Since the original author has not published any workaround results, this is clearly a version diagnosis entry and not a verified fix.

## Problem and symptoms

- Why does the skid-steer example in Gazebo Fortress not turn in the same way as expected on Ubuntu Focal/DART?
- Most of the time, the robot moves straight, and occasionally turns 90°, instead of approximating a circular motion.

## Environment

- Ubuntu 20.04 Focal Docker; Ignition Gazebo Fortress binary; system DART 6.9.2-2build4; official `skid_steer_mecanum.sdf`.

## Priority diagnostics

- Record the exact version of `libdart` and use the same world/command to compare the Bionic Gazebo fork, Focal system DART, or PPA build.

## Possible causes

- The maintainer attributes the difference to the friction support in the Focal system DART; Bionic uses a native Gazebo fork with better support.

## Attempts

- The thread suggests switching to Bionic, building the Gazebo DART fork from source with Ignition, or using the dartsim PPA.

## Effective fixes

- No original author retesting; only the three paths can be considered as the maintainer's suggested workaround.

## Result

- The environment and DART version are confirmed; no trajectory was reported after the workaround was not reported.

- This conclusion does not apply to Bullet, ODE, or current Gazebo/DART versions.
